title: Reduce exact sampler clean work with optimal block checkpoints
body:
**Sampler workspace construction:** the exact denominator-52 finite-window service now uses `559+51*ceil(2*sqrt(L))` clean work bits, with a linear Boolean gate count. It preserves every ordered label, first stopping depth, explicit censor flag and arbitrary-output XOR result from [PR #7773](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7773). All inputs and clean work are restored. **No new kappa** or complete physical sampler is claimed.

Read the [all-L proof and exact bill](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e0d1aa1558583fc06e5a4f14f27e2bb4ffbf3a9/research/inverse52-block-checkpoints/PROOF.md), [full gate generator](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e0d1aa1558583fc06e5a4f14f27e2bb4ffbf3a9/research/inverse52-block-checkpoints/block.py), [certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e0d1aa1558583fc06e5a4f14f27e2bb4ffbf3a9/research/inverse52-block-checkpoints/RESULT.json), [checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e0d1aa1558583fc06e5a4f14f27e2bb4ffbf3a9/research/inverse52-block-checkpoints/verify.py), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e0d1aa1558583fc06e5a4f14f27e2bb4ffbf3a9/research/inverse52-block-checkpoints/SOURCE-PINS.json) and [credits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7e0d1aa1558583fc06e5a4f14f27e2bb4ffbf3a9/research/inverse52-block-checkpoints/CREDITS.md). The consumed source head is `c1fe18fbca499b50c3bbfb12e11218ee9b6acf01`.

| Window | Original clean bits | New clean bits | Original gates | New gates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16 coins | 1,426 | 967 | 34,939 | 58,693 |
| 64 coins | 3,874 | 1,375 | 128,827 | 238,965 |
| 127 coins | 7,087 | 1,732 | 252,055 | 475,729 |

These are complete logical gate and wire counts. The `12+L` read-only parameter/coin wires and `3+bit_length(L+1)` output wires remain separate. Resident coin storage still grows linearly. This is a reduction in additional clean work with more recomputation, not a physical runtime or total-space speedup.

The circuit retains block endpoints and reuses one local history bank. It accumulates each stopping-depth term exactly once while that state is available. It then clears checkpoints in reverse order. The short block goes first; a full last block saves recomputation. Among all partitions in this one-level architecture, the selector first minimizes clean work and then minimizes gates. No optimum over arbitrary circuits or deeper checkpoint schedules is claimed.

For maximum block B, K blocks and last-block length r, there are `D=4*L-2*r` draw-oracle calls. The exact gate count is `3643+977*D+102*(K-1)+2*L`; clean work is `559+51*(B+K)`. The selected partition has `B+K=ceil(2*sqrt(L))`. Preparation, copies, partial blocks, answer extraction and all cleanup are included. The original full-history circuit is an executed positive control.

Python 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/inverse52-block-checkpoints
```

Both modes print this prefix and elapsed seconds:

```text
PASS_INVERSE52_BLOCK_CHECKPOINTS 940486 whole-wire cases 524800 block choices
```

The certificate covers all coin strings for all 2,704 source pairs at L=1,3,4,8; every stopping prefix with both constant suffixes and every live prefix at L=16; named larger-window and alternative-block cases; 524,800 block choices; and all 65,535 ordered partitions through L=16. It checks every wire forwards and backwards. Dirty outputs pass; omitted checkpoint cleanup and a missing boundary-depth term fail. The unchanged preparation and residue arithmetic also run. The full predecessor periodic-edge suite is retained, not rerun.

All 32 source files are authenticated. Normal/optimized registered replay, syntax/indentation, committed bytes/source history/modes, export, sealed read-only Git-free serial replay and publication checks pass. Hosted CI did not certify this package. The [plan job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/44459435773/job/135342333074) failed in the shared `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: the base guide names frontier6030 while the selected record requires `make frontier7000-verify`. The log reports 760 tests, one failure and 24 skipped; package replay was skipped. This package changes no shared CI file. Local replay remains the scientific evidence.

C. H. Bennett supplied [classical reversible checkpointing](https://research.ibm.com/publications/timespace-trade-offs-for-reversible-computation). Ali Romman (@aliromman) supplied the source [finite-window proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c1fe18fbca499b50c3bbfb12e11218ee9b6acf01/research/inverse52-window-circuit/PROOF.md), [gate operations](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c1fe18fbca499b50c3bbfb12e11218ee9b6acf01/research/inverse52-window-circuit/window.py) and [checks](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c1fe18fbca499b50c3bbfb12e11218ee9b6acf01/research/inverse52-window-circuit/verify.py). Nick Petalas (@petalas) supplied the underlying arithmetic gates in [PR #7746](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7746). The [retained credit chain](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/c1fe18fbca499b50c3bbfb12e11218ee9b6acf01/research/inverse52-window-circuit/CREDITS.md) credits JoyboyBrian's actual inverse domain and zxv's decision graph. The related batched-lifting checkpoint work in [PR #3122](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3122) and [PR #3129](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3129) uses a different machine contract; its physical tariff is not transferred.

This remains a censored finite service. Discarding or restarting censored draws is not justified. Unbounded sampling, fresh-coin delivery, owner extraction, tape movement, clean-stock funding and caller installation remain open. No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human or formal-kernel acceptance is claimed. All five assumptions and the selected frontier remain unchanged.
